title: Compute per-feature drift against the reference window
problem: Inputs change gradually and a model rarely fails all at once. Without a per-feature comparison to a reference window, the first sign of drift is a complaint. A statistic applied without thought, though, alerts on noise from small batches or misses shifts in the tails.
context: Builds on validated batches. The learner chooses the drift statistic, for example population stability index or a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, and justifies it for this data. Thresholds live in a data file.
impact: This is the earliest signal the monitor gives. If it is noisy, people learn to ignore it; if it is blind, it is useless.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each numeric feature and the prediction distribution get a drift statistic against the reference window. The choice and its binning or other parameters are justified in the design.
Thresholds per feature are declared in a data file. Changing a threshold changes verdicts with no code change.
A batch below the declared minimum size is reported as not evaluated with the reason, and raises no drift verdict.
When one synthetic feature is shifted, that feature crosses its threshold and unshifted features do not, over repeated seeds.
Automated tests check the statistic against hand-computed values on a small example, the small-batch rule, and single-feature attribution, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains why this statistic fits the data, one rejected alternative, and one kind of real change it would fail to detect.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only. No statistics package.
No network access and no model API. Every input is synthetic and generated or checked in by the learner.
Do not implement label tracking or alerting yet.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: A statistic per feature, data-driven thresholds and an evaluability rule.

investigation_areas: How the chosen statistic behaves on small batches and on shifts confined to the tails
How thresholds are chosen without tuning them to the synthetic incident
What the reference window must contain to be a fair baseline
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design; the learner chooses the runner and the layout.
documentation_requirements: Record the statistic, its parameters, the threshold rationale and the rejected alternative in the learner design.
